Chaque virage du sentier a son couplet,: Every bend of the path has its verse, and whoever knows the song knows the way. The elders walk the children along it.
Chaque convive y a sa place, et c'est pa: Every guest has a place, and it is by the places that the guests are remembered. The head waiter never has a list.
On y discute sans rien noter, pour voir: People talk here without writing anything down, to see what they really know. Someone takes notes anyway, on the sly.
Un cochon qui jongle, une sirène à lunet: A juggling pig, a mermaid in glasses: the stranger the image, the better the shop is remembered. Delivery men no longer get lost.
Un habitant y récite deux mille noms dan: An islander recites two thousand names here in order, then backwards. He swears it is just a method, and nobody believes him.
On y apprend les textes par cœur avant d: Texts are learned by heart here before being copied, page after page. The head first, the parchment after.
Des cercles de papier qu'on fait tourner: Paper circles that are turned to cross ideas. Out come questions nobody had asked.
La maison aux cent pièces: The house of a hundred rooms
Chaque pièce garde un souvenir, posé sur: Each room keeps a memory, set on a piece of furniture. The guide gives the tour with his eyes closed.
Il change les numéros des cargaisons en: He turns cargo numbers into words, and words into stories. He only opens his book to check.
On y apprend des listes qui ne veulent r: Meaningless lists are learned here, to measure how fast they slip away. The curve is posted in the corridor.
Une fiche sue recule d'une case, une fic: A known card moves back one box, a missed card comes back to the front. Pupils revise less, and remember more.
La chambre de celui qui n'oublie rien: The room of the man who forgets nothing
Il retient tout, et peine à faire le tri: He retains everything, and struggles to sort it. The island learned at his house that forgetting is useful too.
Un artisan qui ne retient plus les visag: A craftsman who can no longer remember faces still learns new knacks here. Memory has several drawers.
Le tableau des sept caisses: The board of the seven crates
Le contremaître ne donne jamais plus de: The foreman never gives more than seven instructions at once. The dockers group them in bundles, and everything reaches the right quay.
Avant d'apprendre une règle, on y demand: Before learning a rule, you ask here where it comes from. What you understand here stands up on its own.
Menthe, foin, pain chaud : une bouffée,: Mint, hay, warm bread: one whiff, and a whole memory comes back. The island's elders spend their afternoons here.
Les écoliers s'y posent des questions au: Pupils quiz each other here instead of rereading their exercise books. Those who search for the answer keep it.
Un jeu de cartes battu, deux minutes pou: A shuffled deck of cards, two minutes to memorise it. The island's champions train like runners.
Chaque chenal, chaque écueil, chaque cou: Every channel, every reef, every current known by heart. From learning the coast, their heads have taken its shape.
On y éteint tôt, parce que la nuit range: Lights go out early here, because night tidies away what the day has learned. On the eve of exams, the night watchman confiscates the candles.
